title: A Novel Bio-Inspired Bird Flocking Node Scheduling Algorithm for Dependable Safety-Critical Wireless Sensor Network Systems
content: The Multi-Objective Optimization Problem (MOOP) in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) focuses on optimizing three key objectives: coverage, connectivity, and network lifetime. The MOO problem can be explored using the collective behaviour of the bio-inspired bird flocking model that preserves energy over long migration journeys. Applying such models in WSNs can help achieve the optimisation of the multiple core objectives: coverage, connectivity, and network lifetime. The bird flocking model works collaboratively with Lyapunov function to stabilize the three core objectives mentioned above to solve the MOOP in WSNs. The proposed novel multi-objective bio-inspired bird algorithm is implemented in a MATLAB simulation environment. The achieved results of the novel proposed bio-inspired bird algorithm are evaluated against our previous published work the bio-inspired bat algorithm where the former recorded an enhancement over the latter in many aspects; coverage 8%, connectivity 10%, and network lifetime 80%.
